docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am an undergraduate student currently completing my Bachelor of Science degree in Geographic Information Science & Technology (GIST) at the University of Tennessee Knoxville. I use geospatial analysis to aid in my passion for combining qualitative and quantitative data to research topics in demography, migration, and the environment across various scales. My hands-on experience working with several geospatial tools demonstrate my ability to work with both the technical and theoretical sides of geography.

docs.title: Student Library Assistant — University of Tennessee Knoxville
docs.text:
June 2025 – Present | Knoxville, TN

  • Assist patrons in creative library spaces, including 3D printing, sewing, embroidery, and laser cutting equipment
  • Certify patrons in 3D printing and provide hands-on support for creative projects
  • Coordinate equipment usage and troubleshoot technical issues for diverse user needs

docs.title: Afterschool Volunteer — Centro Hispano de East TN
docs.text:
February 2026 – May 2026 | Knoxville, TN

  • Coordinated and assisted groups of 1st–5th graders with homework and educational activities
  • Supported bilingual learning environments and community engagement for Latino families
  • Facilitated group activities to promote academic success and social development

docs.title: GIS as a Community Tool — Independent Study, University of Tennessee Knoxville
docs.text:
August 2026 – Present | Knoxville, TN

  • Building a GIS model to examine the geographic distribution of traffic "checkpoint" immigration enforcement on the Latino community in Knox County, TN
  • Writing a research paper on the process of creating a community GIS tool, including ethical and informational considerations and potential benefits
  • Collaborating with community stakeholders to ensure participatory and equitable design

docs.title: Glacier Mapping — Independent Research, University of Tennessee Knoxville
docs.text:
January 2026 – Present | Wind River Range, WY

  • Manually mapped over 450 glacier boundaries in the Wind River Range, Wyoming
  • Reconstructed glacier change between 1966–2020 using geomorphic classification techniques
  • Presented research at UTK's Exhibition of Undergraduate Research and Creative Achievement (EURCA) 2026
  • Plans to present at the Geological Society of America's Connects 2026 conference in Denver, Colorado

docs.title: Venice Coastal Flood Vulnerability Project — University of Tennessee Knoxville
docs.text:
October 2025 – December 2025 | Knoxville, TN

  • Calculated and mapped coastal vulnerability based on multiple sea-level rise scenarios using elevation and distance from the coast
  • Worked with Python libraries including geopandas, rasterio, numpy, matplotlib, and shapely
  • Produced spatial analyses and visualizations to assess flood risk in the Venice region
